newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London rally on U.S. election news.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London rally on U.S. election news.

text.p: U.S. shares rallied strongly in London on Wednesday as U.S. elections delivered the hoped for Clinton Presidential win but with Republicans keeping a grip on Congress, traders said.
Worries about a Democrat clean sweep had unnerved markets ahead of the election, concerned about what such an outcome might have meant for fiscal policy in the U.S.

In the event while Bill Clinton comfortably held onto the White House, the Republicans retained control of the Senate and House of Representatives, lifting hopes that a lid would be kept on government spending.
Bonds and the dollar rallied on the news and Wall Street stocks were also expected to open strongly as fears about a runaway government spending programme faded.
"Stocks are up across the board here in London. Bonds have also rallied and we look set to bounce in New York at the open - maybe 20, 30 points," said one trader.
Drug stocks were particularly bouyant as concerns about a radical overhaul of the healthcare system receded.
But dealers were cautious about the prospects of a prolonged spike in share prices and predicted profit-taking would emerge later in the session.

U.S. shares had largely discounted the outcome, said traders, and in the last two sessions the Dow had added around 20 and 40 points respectively. It finished Tuesday at 6,081.18, just 13 points off its all-time closing high of October 18.

"The only thing that was preying on people's minds was whether the Republicans would hold onto Congress. The futures and long bond are both trading higher, not as strongly as they were in Asia but they're still ahead," said a trader.
"We may see shares drift after the inital advance but no sharp profit-taking. There was some degree of position-taking prior to the election but any sell-off should be muted."
Stock markets advanced across the board in Europe on the election results, with leading shares in London adding over 1/2 percent, breaking a series of disappointing sessions.
German shares also rallied, rising 38.95 points to 2,730.24 while in France the CAC 40 index gained 21.22 points to 2,208.53.

In the Far East, Japan soared 399.19 points - 1.94 percent - to close at 20,991.52 as the dollar recovered to the 114 yen level and in Hong Kong shares surged 272.77 points to a record high of 12,779.11.
